text: This man sells bananas in Mumbai. He takes digital payments all day, with no card machine and no fees.
So how did a country that ran on cash get here?
In 2016, India paid for almost everything in cash.
साहब, केले बेचता हूँ, बैंक नहीं चलाता।
Card machines cost money, and banks take a cut, so small shops said no.
That April, India's banks launched U P I. Any bank to any bank, by phone, in seconds, for free.
Hardly anyone used it. Then, on November eighth, India cancelled its five hundred and thousand rupee notes overnight.
About eighty six percent of India's cash stopped being money.
Suddenly, people had no choice. And a Q R code costs nothing to print.
Today, U P I handles more than twenty billion payments a month. And most of them start with a sticker like this one.
